review.summary:
The typed-preservation chunk delivers the substance of plan item 3. `tools/generate_models.py:471-506` marks vendor-added fields as `vendorProjection` (set in `tools/red_team_dataplane.py:402`), refuses non-optional projections (`:472`), and emits a hand-written `Deserialize` that tries each added field's typed projection and, on failure, re-inserts the untouched wire value so it lands in the model's existing `Extensions` storage. The matching `Serialize` keeps baseline-field collisions as hard errors (projection names are excluded from `KNOWN`, `:498-499`) and suppresses the raw extension entry when the typed field is explicitly set, so an explicit replacement cannot emit duplicate JSON keys. Evidence is genuinely executed and ledger-driven: `contracts/compatibility/g25/projections.json` is derived directly from `augment_models`' additions list (`tools/g25_fixtures.py:89`), the Rust match arms are generated from it and `--check`-guarded (`tools/g25_fixtures.py:100-112`), and `crates/scm-sdk/tests/g25_response_compatibility.rs:336-361` round-trips all 55 added fields × 6 null/wrong-type/nested-extra mutations, including anonymous nested and union-variant models. The 15381-case root test (`:67-125`) additionally round-trips whole responses through the typed decoders in both response modes. `cargo fmt/check/clippy -D warnings/test/doc` passed on 1.89.0 and 1.99.0 with the `red-team` feature (162s and 177s), and all generator/audit/oracle/governance suites passed.

Two substantive problems block acceptance. First, the generated projection codec abandons the crate's own JSON decoding boundary: it uses `serde_json::Map::deserialize` and `serde_json::from_value` into a `#[serde(flatten)]`-bearing `BaselineWire` struct, whereas every other generated decode path routes through `crate::json_decode::from_value` (see the generator's own intersection template at `tools/generate_models.py:215` and `models/support.rs:111-115`). `crates/scm-sdk/src/json_decode.rs:1-8` and `:266-311` exist precisely because, under `serde_json/arbitrary_precision`, `Value::deserialize_any` can issue 128-bit visits that Serde's intermediate `Content` buffer cannot hold. These 25 models previously derived `Deserialize` and were reached through that workaround; they no longer are, so an unknown (flattened) response field holding a 128-bit integer now fails to decode where it previously succeeded — the exact "new vendor value must not fail an old operation" class this chunk fixes. No CI feature set combines `red-team` with `serde_json/arbitrary_precision` (`scripts/check-rust.py:20-28`; `.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:90`), and the test file is `#![cfg(feature = "red-team")]`, so nothing exercises or documents this. Second, the headline projection test asserts only wire-value identity; because the fallback also round-trips identically, it cannot distinguish "typed projection populated" from "always fell back to extensions" for 54 of the 55 fields — a decoder that never populated any projection would still show green.

findings.description: The generated projection deserializer decodes the baseline remainder with raw `serde_json::from_value(serde_json::Value::Object(raw))` into a struct carrying `#[serde(flatten)] extensions`, instead of `crate::json_decode::from_value`. `crates/scm-sdk/src/json_decode.rs:1-8` and `:266-311` document that this module exists to keep `Value::deserialize_any` from issuing 128-bit visits into Serde's `Content` buffer under `serde_json/arbitrary_precision`, and the generator itself uses `crate::json_decode::from_value` on every other owned-value decode path (`tools/generate_models.py:215-216`, `crates/scm-sdk/src/models/support.rs:111-115`, `crates/scm-sdk/src/data.rs:115,176`). Before this chunk the 25 affected models derived `Deserialize` and inherited that workaround; they no longer do, so under feature unification an unknown/flattened response field holding a 128-bit integer makes the whole model fail to decode. That is a passthrough regression of exactly the class this chunk is meant to fix, and it is silent in the recorded evidence because no feature set combines `red-team` with `serde_json/arbitrary_precision` (`scripts/check-rust.py:20-28`, `.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:90`) and the test file is gated on `red-team` (`crates/scm-sdk/tests/g25_response_compatibility.rs:2`).
findings.required_fix: Route the projection codec through the crate's JSON boundary: replace `serde_json::from_value` at tools/generate_models.py:495 and :489 with `crate::json_decode::from_value`, and avoid materializing through `serde_json::Map`/`serde_json::Value` in a way that drops the `OwnedValue` deserializer (tools/generate_models.py:486). Then add an executed check that decodes at least one projection-bearing model under `serde_json/arbitrary_precision` with a 128-bit-integer unknown field — e.g. a `red-team-json-unification` feature set in scripts/check-rust.py plus the corresponding CI matrix entry — and regenerate crates/scm-sdk/src/models/generated.rs.

findings.description: `every_vendor_added_projection_preserves_absence_null_and_unrepresentable_values` asserts only `projection_roundtrip(name, input) == input`. Both decode outcomes round-trip identically (typed field set, or raw value preserved in `Extensions`), so the test cannot distinguish a working typed projection from a decoder that always falls back to extension storage; it also cannot distinguish `Patch::Null` from a null preserved as an extension for nullable projections. Only one field (`AttackOutput.judge_reasoning`, :402-424) asserts the actual fallback/typed state. For the other 54 rows the chunk's central claim — that vendor-added fields are usable typed projections and not merely preserved bytes — is unverified by the recorded evidence.
findings.required_fix: Extend contracts/compatibility/g25/projections.json with a schema-derived conforming witness per row and a nullability flag, and generate a per-type assertion (alongside the existing `projection_roundtrip` arms in tools/g25_fixtures.py:100-102) that for the conforming witness the extension map does not contain the field key, and that for a null input a nullable projection yields `Patch::Null` while a non-nullable projection falls back to extension storage.

findings.description: When a caller sets a projection field and also inserts an extension under the same wire key, the serializer silently skips the extension entry. For response models this is the documented precedence rule (docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md:15), but the same codec is generated for request-named models — `JobCreateRequestJobMetadataVariant1/2/3` are projection-bearing (contracts/compatibility/g25/projections.json:540-578) and are reached only through `JobCreateRequest.job_metadata` (crates/scm-sdk/src/models/generated.rs:144310). There, the rule silently discards caller-supplied request data, and nothing classifies these models as request-side or records that the response-oriented fallback intentionally applies to them.
findings.required_fix: Record a request/response classification per projection row in contracts/compatibility/g25/projections.json and assert the request-named entries are the intentional reviewed set in tools/test_g25_generation.py; either make a projection/extension collision an explicit serialization error for request-side models or document the precedence rule for requests in docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md.

findings.description: The baseline decode failure is collapsed to `map_err(|_| serde::de::Error::custom("baseline response model mismatch"))`, discarding serde's field/path detail for all 25 projection-bearing models while every other generated model surfaces the detailed message. The public boundary already flattens to `ErrorKind::Validation` (crates/scm-sdk/src/models/support.rs:112-115), so user-visible impact is limited, but internal and nested-context diagnosis of which baseline field mismatched is lost. The per-field `value.clone()` at :489 also clones every projection value on the success path purely to serve the error path.
findings.required_fix: Preserve the underlying serde error text in the custom message at tools/generate_models.py:495, and avoid the unconditional `value.clone()` at :489 (for example by decoding from a borrowed deserializer or cloning only when the typed decode fails).

findings.description: A Python dict is interpolated directly into the generated report, so docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md:33 renders `{'rfc3339': 56, 'uuid': 124, 'duration': 4}` in user-facing Markdown. Out of this chunk's three scope artifacts but inside the phase's scope evidence and the same generation pipeline whose `--check` passed.
findings.required_fix: Format the occurrence counts as prose or a Markdown list in tools/g25_report.py:118 and regenerate docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md.

evidence: docs/reviews/phase-19-chunk-typed-preservation-attempt-01.checks.json records 17 executed checks, all exit_code 0, with plausible wall-clock durations, including `python tools/generate_models.py --check` (2.94s, `{"checked": true, "outputs": 16, "graphNodes": 13018}`), `python tools/g25_fixtures.py --check` (0.825s, `{"roots": 46, "mutations": 15381, "formats": 184, "enums": 138, "typedProjectionFields": 55}`), and `tools/node_modules/.bin/tsx tools/g25-oracle.mts --check` (2.524s, `{"roots":46,"independentOutcomes":15381}`). These are executed, not asserted.

scripts/check-rust.py was executed for toolchains 1.89.0 and 1.99.0 with `--feature-set red-team`; each record lists six commands (fmt, check --all-targets, clippy -D warnings, test, test --examples, doc) all at exit_code 0, taking 162.478s and 176.977s. `crates/scm-sdk/tests/g25_response_compatibility.rs:2` is `#![cfg(feature = "red-team")]`, so the chunk's Rust regressions did run under both compilers.

Projection marking and the fail-closed guard are real: tools/red_team_dataplane.py:402 sets `vendorProjection: True` on fields absent from the frozen object, wrapping non-optional vendor schemas in `ZodOptional` first (:398-401); tools/generate_models.py:471-473 collects those names and raises `ValueError("Vendor response projections must remain optional")` if any projection is required.

The generated codec matches the plan: crates/scm-sdk/src/models/generated.rs:6028-6036 shows `audio_technique` attempted as `Patch<String>` with the raw value re-inserted into `raw` on failure; :6091-6095 shows the flattened `BaselineWire` decode; :6135-6162 shows `KNOWN` containing only the 26 baseline wire names and omitting `threat_details`, `audio` and `audio_technique`, so baseline-field extension collisions error while a preserved projection value serializes once.

Evidence is ledger-driven and cannot silently shrink: tools/g25_fixtures.py:89 builds every projections.json row directly from `augment_models`' returned additions, :100-102 regenerates the Rust `projection_roundtrip` arms from those rows, and :110-111 fails with 'G25 generated fixture/binding is stale' on drift. contracts/compatibility/g25/projections.json holds 55 rows over 25 distinct Rust types, matching both the 25 `baseline response model mismatch` occurrences in generated.rs and the 25 generated match arms, and `crates/scm-sdk/tests/g25_response_compatibility.rs:339` pins `rows.len() == 55`.

Whole-response typed coverage exists beyond the per-field test: crates/scm-sdk/tests/g25_response_compatibility.rs:109-123 validates each of the 15381 cases in both response modes, calls `preserve` on the result, and asserts `roundtrip(schema, result) == result` through the operation's public return type, so projection fallback nested in arrays and untagged unions is exercised against independent Zod outcomes.

The json_decode divergence is verifiable from the repository's own sources: crates/scm-sdk/src/json_decode.rs:1-8 states the module exists because 'serde_json's arbitrary_precision Numbers may emit i128/u128 from Value::deserialize_any, which Serde's intermediate Content visitor cannot buffer', and :285-311 implements that routing. crates/scm-sdk/src/models/support.rs:111-115 and :266-269, plus crates/scm-sdk/src/data.rs:115 and :176, all use `crate::json_decode::from_value`; tools/generate_models.py:486, :489 and :495 use raw `serde_json` instead.

No executed check covers that path: scripts/check-rust.py:21 defines `json-unification` as `--no-default-features --features serde_json/arbitrary_precision` and :26 defines `gateway-json-unification`; neither enables `red-team`, `all` is `--all-features` (:20) which does not enable an optional dependency feature, and .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:90 lists no red-team/arbitrary_precision combination. grep for 'unification' or 'arbitrary' in docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md returns no matches, so the gap is also undocumented.

Governance tooling is independently exercised: the checks file records 37 passing tests in tools/test_review_phase.py, including `test_phase_and_chunk_thresholds`, `test_categories_cannot_be_fabricated`, `test_blockers_still_block_fifth_attempt` and `test_fifth_exception_is_explicit_and_requires_deficiency`, plus 14 passing tools/test_g25*.py tests and 11 passing tools/test_model_generation.py generation guards.

docs/phase-status.json:3 records `active_phase: 19`; :3771-3784 lists the three phase-19 chunks all at `implemented_awaiting_checks_and_review` with `reviews: []`, so no prior acceptance is being claimed for this chunk.

docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md:15 documents the behaviour under review ('Optional vendor-added typed projections preserve unsupported JSON in extension storage when the typed field cannot represent it. An explicitly set typed field supersedes that fallback. Baseline-field extension collisions remain errors.'), and :182 honestly records that the 17 reported airs-cli-rs loopback tests were not executed here.
limitations: Bash is unavailable in this session, so I could not recompute the reviewed source SHA256 (e5a0d96...) or the checks-file hash (f3183a7...), nor re-execute any command. Check outcomes are assessed from the recorded stdout/stderr, exit codes and durations in docs/reviews/phase-19-chunk-typed-preservation-attempt-01.checks.json, which are internally consistent and non-trivial, but I verified them as records rather than by re-running them.

The high finding is derived by construction from the repository's own documentation of the Serde `Content` 128-bit limitation (crates/scm-sdk/src/json_decode.rs:1-8, :266-311) plus the generated code path, not from an observed failing run; I could not build the crate under `serde_json/arbitrary_precision` with `red-team` to demonstrate the error empirically. That no such build exists anywhere in the recorded checks or CI matrix is itself part of the finding.

I reviewed the three chunk scope artifacts in depth (tools/generate_models.py, crates/scm-sdk/src/models/generated.rs, crates/scm-sdk/tests/g25_response_compatibility.rs) and read the supporting phase artifacts (plan, PHASES.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, phase-status.json, projections.json, g25_fixtures.py, G25_COMPATIBILITY.md, json_decode.rs, data.rs, models/support.rs, red_team_dataplane.py). generated.rs is ~183k lines; I inspected the projection codecs by targeted grep plus full reads of the AttackDetailResponse and StreamDetailResponseGoal regions, not every one of the 25 generated impls.

I did not re-audit the validation-policy or regression-and-governance chunks, phase 18's accepted plan/audit, or historical release infrastructure, per the scoping instruction. Findings in tools/g25_report.py and contracts/compatibility/g25/projections.json are reported only where they bear directly on this chunk's evidence.
Live service acceptance and the 17 reported airs-cli-rs loopback failures remain unverified; the plan and docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md:182 state this explicitly and I make no claim either way.
